nodes.label: API Key Auth Model
nodes.rationale: For a trusted server caller you control the relationship with (the main CRM). One key currently grants access to every API-key domain since there is only one external caller today; per-domain scoping is deliberately deferred as speculative until a second, less-trusted caller exists.

nodes.label: Optional API Key Auth Model
nodes.rationale: For sites with no backend of their own there is nowhere safe to hold a secret, so requiring one would create false security; an invalid/revoked key still returns 401 rather than silently downgrading to anonymous, so a real integration bug (typo'd env var, revoked key) isn't hidden.

nodes.label: Per-Site trackingId/apiSecret Auth Model
nodes.rationale: Website Intelligence needs a distinct matching credential pair per tracked site, not one global key, because it must attribute a lead to that specific site's visitor/session/UTM data rather than just authenticate a generic caller.

nodes.label: Adding a New External API Domain — Standard Pattern
nodes.rationale: External-facing endpoints are kept physically separate from internal controllers/routes because they use different auth models (never JWT), have a different audience (a contract with a system you don't control, changing it means coordinating with another team), and need different docs (a human on the other team, not just the calling frontend code) — mixing them risks accidentally leaving a partner-facing route unprotected or JWT-gated by mistake.

nodes.label: Production-Grade Notification Architecture Blueprint
nodes.rationale: Explicitly marked NOT YET IMPLEMENTED: the current system is only Socket.io + MongoDB-persisted notifications with a simple notificationPrefs Map on User; this document is an aspirational future direction (web-push/VAPID, BullMQ-driven notification queue, NotificationPreference schema), not shipped behavior.

nodes.label: API 401 Intercept + Auto-Refresh
nodes.rationale: Concurrent failed requests are queued during a token refresh and replayed afterward, rather than each firing its own refresh call, to avoid refresh races; a failed refresh dispatches crm:logout so the app can react globally.

nodes.label: Single Zustand Store Pattern
nodes.rationale: All frontend domain state (auth, users, messages/channels/DMs, tasks, todos, clients, leads, meetings, notifications, timer, UI state) lives in one ~1500-line store because these domains interact heavily (e.g. socket events must update multiple domains at once); it is called out as the most important file in the frontend.

nodes.label: Timer/Worklog Sync via sendBeacon
nodes.rationale: Timer/worklog state is synced to /api/worklog via navigator.sendBeacon() on beforeunload specifically so work time is not lost when a tab closes.

nodes.label: Unread Count Persistence via localStorage
nodes.rationale: Unread counts are persisted in localStorage keyed crm_unread_{userId} so badge counts survive page reloads.

nodes.label: Redis + BullMQ Queueing for Notification Delivery
nodes.rationale: Template rendering, SMTP connections, and push requests are block-heavy, so delivery is offloaded from the main Express server to a Redis/BullMQ queue and dedicated workers to keep API response times sub-100ms; BullMQ's exponential-backoff retries ensure no notification is lost if a delivery service is temporarily down.
nodes.norm_label: redis + bullmq queueing for notification delivery

nodes.label: Rate Limiting & Digest Aggregation
nodes.rationale: Web Push and Email are throttled and bursts are aggregated into a single digest (e.g. 10 DMs in 1 minute while offline becomes one 'you have 10 unread messages' email) to prevent spam rather than sending one notification per event.
